''Casapianos'' (The ones from Casa Pia) | short name = Casa Pia | owner = Robert Platek | chairman = Victor Franco | chrtitle = President | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Filipe Coelho (football manager, born 1985)|Filipe Coelho]] | founded = {{Start date and age|df=yes|3 July 1920}} | ground = [[Estádio Pina Manique]], [[Lisbon]] | capacity = 6,000 | league = [[Primeira Liga]] | season = [[2025–26 Primeira Liga|2025–26]] | position = Primeira Liga, 16th of 18 | current = 2026–27 Casa Pia A.C. season | website = {{URL|https://casapiaac.pt/}} | pattern_la1 = _casapia2627h | pattern_b1 = _casapia2627h | pattern_ra1 = _casapia2627h | pattern_sh1 = _casapia2627h | pattern_so1 = _casapia2627hl | leftarm1 = 000000 | body1 = 000000 | rightarm1 = 000000 | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_la2 = _casapia2627a | pattern_b2 = _casapia2627a | pattern_ra2 = _casapia2627a | pattern_sh2 = _casapia2627a | pattern_so2 = _casapia2627al | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = FFFFFF | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = FFFFFF | socks2 = FFFFFF | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} '''Casa Pia Atlético Clube''', commonly known as '''Casa Pia''', is a Portuguese multi-[[sport]]s club founded in 1920 and based in [[Lisbon]], Portugal, best known for its professional [[football team]], that competes in the [[Primeira Liga]]. The club is named after [[Casa Pia]], a Portuguese children's [[Charitable organization|charity]], and many of its athletes come from that institution. Its football stadium is ''Estádio Pina Manique'', named in honor of [[Pina Manique]], the founder of Casa Pia children's charity. Casa Pia AC was one of the most versatile Portuguese clubs, having played 25 sports, with the curiosity of having been the only one who practiced [[baseball]] regularly, beating the strong team of the American Colony on 4 July 1923 at [[Campo das Laranjeiras]] by 25–24.{{Cite web |url=https://casapiaac.pt/clube/historia-e-palmares/ |title=História e Palmarés – Casa Pia Atlético Clube |trans-title=History and Honours – Casa Pia Atlético Clube |language=pt |website=casapiaac.pt |accessdate=15 October 2022 |archive-date=24 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220824115631/https://casapiaac.pt/clube/historia-e-palmares/ |url-status=dead }} On 18 December 1921, when [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] made their international debut against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in [[Madrid]], Casa Pia FC provided the squad with four players in a 1–3 loss, including [[Cândido de Oliveira]], who was the [[Captain (association football)|team captain]]. Casa Pia promoted from Serie E of [[Terceira Divisão]] to Centre Group of [[Portuguese Second Division]] in 2009–10 season as champions.{{Cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/national/portugal/iii-divisao/2009-2010/group-e---promotion/ |title=Summary - III Divisão - Portugal - Results, fixtures, tables and news - Soccerway |website=int.soccerway.com}}{{citation needed|date=August 2025}} They were promoted again to [[LigaPro]] in 2019. After a hiatus of 83 years, the team were promoted to the [[Primeira Liga]] in the 2022–23 season."}}
